problem_clarity.rationale: Problem statement is clearly articulated: students struggle with 3D molecular structure understanding due to 2D teaching materials (flat textbook illustrations, 2D diagrams on boards), which leads to mechanical memorization without deep understanding of spatial structure, chemical bonds, valence angles, and atomic positioning

scope_boundedness.rationale: MVP scope is well-defined with clear boundaries: (1) formula parsing for simple inorganic/organic molecules (H2O, CH4, C2H6O, C6H12O6); (2) 3D visualization with correct geometry (bonds, valence angles); (3) basic interactivity (rotation, zoom, pan); (4) atomic annotations (H, C, O, N); (5) browser accessibility without installation. Explicit NOT items: no macromolecules (proteins, DNA), no chemical simulations (dynamics, reactions), no authorization/saving systems, no mobile apps

stakeholder_coverage.rationale: Stakeholders are well-identified across the educational ecosystem: middle school students (grades 7-9, ages 12-15) studying basic chemistry with simple molecules (H2O, CO2, NH3); high school students (grades 10-11, ages 15-17) studying organic chemistry with complex molecules (ethanol, benzene); chemistry teachers for classroom demonstrations; school administration (accessibility requirements, no paid subscriptions); parents (educational value, safety expectations); developers (support and maintenance requirements)

assumption_visibility.rationale: Assumptions are clearly documented about technical and educational constraints: target audience has modern browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari) on school computers or personal devices; users lack technical skills requiring intuitive interface; school laptops have basic WebGL support (Intel HD Graphics or similar); internet access in schools may be limited requiring offline-first design after initial load; application supplements textbooks not replacing teachers; users input formulas in standard chemical notation (H2O, C2H5OH)

unknowns_manageability.rationale: Critical unknowns remain unresolved and are blocking for development decisions: real WebGL quality on school devices (unknown which GPUs schools use and actual performance); molecular geometry data accuracy (unclear sources for correct atomic coordinates - libraries, databases, calculations); formula parsing effectiveness (unclear complexity of parsing organic formulas with structural ambiguity like C2H6O → ethanol vs dimethyl ether); essential feature priorities (unknown which interactive features are most important - distance measurement, angle measurement, structural formulas); competition landscape (unclear if similar free tools exist for schools); curriculum integration (unclear how application integrates with existing lesson plans); scalability requirements (unclear user count and infrastructure needs)

risk_visibility.rationale: Risks are comprehensively identified and categorized across multiple dimensions: Technical - WebGL performance on weak devices (old school laptops), impossible correct display of complex molecules without optimization, formula parsing errors (molecular structure ambiguity); Educational - incorrect molecular geometry may misinform students, application may be perceived as game not educational tool, teachers may not adopt due to lack of methodological materials; Adoption - schools may block external resource access, accessibility requirements (visually impaired, mobile devices), localization requirements (Russian and other languages); Support - regular updates needed for molecular data, user bug reports requiring feedback mechanism, potential server load (if backend used)

evidence_grounding.rationale: Evidence refs are entirely prospective - they describe research plans rather than actual collected evidence. Refs mention what SHOULD be done (teacher surveys, prototype testing, technical performance testing, library comparison, existing material analysis, competitive analysis of MolView/ChemSketch/Kmol, MVP pilot with 5-10 basic molecules) but not what WAS actually collected or measured. No actual research results, user feedback, performance benchmarks, or technical validation data are provided

blocking_gaps.description: All evidence references are research plans (what should be done) rather than actual collected evidence (what was found). No actual user research, technical testing, or competitive analysis results are provided to validate the problem, solution, or implementation feasibility
No actual WebGL performance data from school devices. Unknown which GPUs are used in schools and their real rendering performance for 3D molecular visualization

No validation of formula parsing feasibility for organic molecules with structural ambiguity (e.g., C2H6O could be ethanol or dimethyl ether). Unclear if parsing can be implemented correctly without user guidance
No actual teacher or student feedback collected. Unclear if real demand exists from chemistry teachers and students, or if existing free tools already address the problem adequately

non_blocking_gaps.description: Molecular geometry data source needs clarification but can be resolved during development (existing libraries like molstar, 3Dmol.js, or open molecular databases)
Essential interactive features need prioritization through user research but can be deferred to post-MVP iterations based on actual usage patterns

payload.rationale: The proposal demonstrates strong problem clarity, well-defined scope, comprehensive stakeholder coverage, visible assumptions, and thorough risk identification. However, two critical dimensions are insufficient: (1) Evidence grounding is entirely prospective with no actual research data collected; (2) Unknowns manageability is insufficient with multiple blocking unknowns unresolved. The recommended outcome 'clarify' in the rationale aligns with this assessment - the proposal needs targeted investigation (technical prototyping for WebGL performance, teacher surveys for demand validation, competitive analysis for positioning) before development commitment. The confidence is moderate-low (0.4) due to strong foundation but critical evidence gaps blocking implementation decisions
